column2: How do I find out what language a record is written in, or write in Cyrillic or Greek?
column3: Settings → Calendar / measures → “Alphabets and languages of records”. “🔤 A language” shows the alphabet of 40 languages (accented letters, old letters such as the long s ſ, Latin abbreviations, transliteration of Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew and Arabic) and how to recognise it. “🔎 Which language?”: type a letter or a word from the record (ł, ő, ж, natus…), the possible languages are shown, the most likely first. “⌨️ Cyrillic and Greek”: a small keyboard to write a name, copy it and read it in Latin letters.

column2: How do I convert an old date (Republican calendar, Julian…)?
column3: Settings → Calendar / measures → “Convert a date”: 26 calendars, including the Republican, the Julian, the Roman (calends, nones, ides) and the English Old Style.

It is installed only once: Settings → Handwriting recognition (HTR). A 3-step assistant says what is missing and why: ① the engine (Kraken, with a ready-made Python that the app downloads itself: nothing for you to install), ② the handwriting model, ③ the check (“✓ Ready: handwriting reading”). If there is a problem, the message says what to do depending on your computer (Mac, Windows, Linux), then “↻ Try again”.

column2: Read the record: how do I automatically read a handwritten record?
column3: In the transcription workshop (“📜 Workshop” on an image, or Lists → Editing tools → “📜 Record transcription”): “✨ Read the record”. The app finds the lines and reads the whole page, or only the chosen area (draw it with ▭, then “✨ Read this area”). Reading happens in the background, on your computer, without the Internet: you can keep working (“■ Stop” to interrupt it). Then the text is offered line by line next to its piece of image; uncertain words are highlighted in yellow: click them to correct them, Enter goes to the next line. “✓ Put the lines in the text” adds them (with one area per line), then names, dates and places are spotted by themselves. “↻ Read again with this model” tries another model.

column2: Which handwriting model should I choose to read my records?
column3: Settings → Handwriting recognition (HTR), step ②: “McCATMuS” (recommended) for parish registers and French civil registration from the 17th to the 19th century, letters and today’s handwriting; “CATMuS Medieval” for Latin and old scripts (before 1500). Each model downloads in one click from its official source (zenodo.org); its licence (CC BY 4.0: free, crediting the authors) is read at the source and the file is checked by its fingerprint before being kept. For other languages, add a .mlmodel file by hand (“📁 Choose the file…”).

column2: How do I uninstall handwriting reading?
column3: Settings → Handwriting recognition (HTR) → “🗑 Uninstall…”: the engine (≈ 1.5 GB) is deleted from the data folder; you can keep the models to reinstall faster. Transcriptions already made stay. A single model is removed with “🗑 Remove” (and “↶ Undo” puts it back).

column2: How do I make a backup?
column3: Settings → “🗓 Automatic backup”: “💾 Back up now” (or ⌘⇧B) makes one straight away, and the page sets up the copies made automatically. The full backup with all the media in a single file, password-protected if you like, is in Settings → Clean export.

column2: How do I set up automatic backup (every day, on a USB stick, in iCloud or Dropbox)?
column3: Settings → “🗓 Automatic backup”. When: every N hours, every day or every week, and “Also when closing the app” (only if something has changed). Where: write the folder (a USB stick, an external disk, or an iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive… folder: it is just a folder, the app uses no online service); empty = in the app’s folder, on the same disk. What: how many copies to keep (10 at first: the oldest automatic copy is deleted), with or without the media (copied once, then only the new ones), and all your genealogies if you have several (each in its subfolder). Each copy is a clean snapshot of the database, checked (integrity check) before it gets its name. Everything is kept by itself; “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left. If the stick is unplugged, a message says so, without blocking anything, and the copy is made as soon as it comes back. “Last backup: …” is shown at the top of the page and in the dashboard’s “🗓 Automatic backup” widget.

column2: How do I go back to a backup?
column3: Settings → “🗓 Automatic backup” → “The copies”: each copy shows its date, its size and “CHECKED” (or “DAMAGED”). “↺ Go back to this copy” replaces your genealogy with this one, after a question (it cannot be undone with one click). Your previous database is first kept in the backups, under a name ending in “avant-restauration”, never deleted by itself: you can go back to it the same way. A damaged copy is refused.

column2: How do I have my genealogy on two computers (the laptop and the office one)?
column3: Settings → Working together → “🔄 Two computers”. Choose a shared folder: a USB stick, or an iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive… folder (no server, no online service from the app), then “🔗 Link this folder”: the app puts a starting copy there, “depart.db”. On the other computer, open “depart.db” (start screen → Import a file, or a new empty genealogy), then choose the same folder at the same place. After that, “🔄 Synchronise” (or automatically on opening and every 15 minutes): each computer drops its changes in the folder and takes those of the other — records, families, events, places, notes, sources, citations, media (with the photo file). Just after, “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before; the undone changes are “set aside” and “Review” lets you choose them one by one. Not yet exchanged: the other tools (Workshop, boards, houses, animal tracking…) and the app settings.

column2: Two computers: the same record was changed on both sides, what should I do?
column3: Everything else is merged by itself; only these records wait for you in Settings → Working together → “🔄 Two computers”, side by side: your version on the left, the other computer’s on the right, only what differs. “Keep mine” (your version goes back to the other one), “Take the other” (it replaces yours), and for a note, “Keep both” (the other’s note is added alongside, with the name of its computer in the title). “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left if you made a mistake.

column2: The app says “Genealogy open elsewhere”: what should I do?
column3: Your database is stored in a folder that two computers can see (iCloud, Dropbox, a network drive…) and the other computer has opened it: if both wrote to this file at the same time, it could be damaged. Close the app on the other computer, then “↻ Try again”. If the other computer is off or the app stopped abruptly there, “Open anyway” (the app also does it by itself after 5 minutes without any sign of life). To really work in two places, use “🔄 Two computers”: each keeps its own database, and changes go through a shared folder.

column2: How do I send the tree to the family without risk of it being changed (Share with the family)?
column3: Settings → Export → “📤 Share with the family…”: choose the branches (nothing = the whole database), what happens to living people (hidden, or first name only) and what is shown (photos, records, notes). The summary “Here is what goes out” updates before the .zip file is made. The family unzips it and opens index.html with a double-click: the tree, the records, the photos and the search, without the app or the Internet, and nothing can be changed. Confidential records never go out, nor a photo showing a living person; the full name of a living person written in a note is replaced by “[name removed]”.

column2: How do I keep a copy at a cousin’s?
column3: Settings → Copy at a cousin’s: the copy is encrypted, they keep it without being able to read it and give it back to you if your computer breaks down.

column2: How do I ask a cousin or an aunt for their memories?
column3: Lists → 💬 Questions for relatives → “＋ New questionnaire” (or “💬 Ask questions about her” on a record, or “💬 Questionnaire” in the Directory of the living). Choose the recipient, a title, a welcome message and ready-made questions (childhood, house and village, occupations, war, celebrations, recipes, photos “Who is in this photo?”, a specific person) or your own; arrange them with ⠿. On the right, the preview as your relative will see it. “⤓ Download the questionnaire” makes a single .html file to attach to an e-mail (“📋 Copy the message” gives the text): it opens in their browser, without the Internet, keeps their answers as they go, and “⤓ Save my answers” gives them a small file to send back to you. “🖨 Printable version”: lines to answer by hand.

column2: How do I bring a relative’s answers into my genealogy?
column3: Lists → 💬 Questions for relatives → “⤒ Import the answers”: drop the .json file they sent back, then choose for each answer where it goes: “💬 Testimony” on the record of the person concerned (“Testimonies / memories” block), “📖 Family memory” (recipe, tradition, story…) or “Do not import”. Their name and the date go automatically into “Where it comes from”. An answer received by plain e-mail: “✎ Paste an answer” on the questionnaire’s page. “↶ Undo” removes everything that has just come in. Only files from a questionnaire you sent are accepted.

column2: How do two people work on the same genealogy?
column3: Settings → Working together: you start from the same database, then exchange packages of changes, accepted or refused one by one.

column2: How do I make a short video montage?
column3: Lists → 🎬 Videos → “🎬 Montage” (far right), or “✂️ Edit” on a video. Five tracks: 🎬 Video 1 (the clips one after another, each with its transition: cross-fade, through black, through white), 🖼️ Video 2 (a video inset in a corner), 🔤 Texts (still or moving titles: fade, slide, rise, grow, scrolling credits, typewriter; font, size, colour, banner, position), 🎵 Sound 1 and Sound 2 (music, voice). “🔊 Detach the sound” puts a clip’s sound on a separate track, to move it, lower it or remove it. 🎨 Colours tab: brightness, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint and ready-made styles (Old film, Black and white…), for the whole film or a single clip. Click the timeline to position yourself, drag the insets, texts and sounds. “⤓ Export the video…” replays the montage and makes a file of it (MP4 or WebM); “💾 Save the project” keeps the montage to continue it later.

column2: How do I save a montage to continue it later?
column3: In the montage: “💾 Save the project” (or ⌘S; ⇧⌘S for a copy under another name). Files imported from the computer are then sent to Media. To reopen it: “📂 Projects…” at the bottom of the montage, or Lists → Videos → “🎬 Montage”, which offers your projects (open, rename, delete) or a new montage. “⤓ Export the video…” makes the video file, without closing the montage.
